title: Toledo — Equation Library of the Human–AI Readout Programme
description: The permanent, coded registry of every equation in the Human–AI Readout Programme together with its Coq (Th_coqc) formalisation. Th_coqc certifies that a lemma is closed under a stated finite model's global context — an internal-consistency check, never an empirical or physical truth claim. v1.5 registers 23 readings (RET-N01–23) and 23 occurrences on existing codes from the deposited paper 'The Recursive Epistemic Tunnel' v2.1 (10.5281/zenodo.22639311) — 990 entries total — and closes a debt pass across the registry: the 52 status:unverified entries were re-checked at source and kept as unverified with a dated note; 111 tier values were quoted from source text; 210 wrapped_related Coq entries were examined for a derivable independent closure, none qualified, and each was kept wrapped_related with its reason recorded; 119 Theta/CMC entries gained Toledo-native Coq files (116 closed, 3 carrying a named axiom) and 78 further Coq files were written for Effort, Economics of Expertise, Core Epistemic Structure and Tunnel readings; the CMC root's connection to a Genesis root was searched for at source, none was found, and a labelled proposition was drafted for the founder to confirm or reject. Ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and command-line client (19 tools over stdio, a SQLite/FTS5 search index, and a static read API published on GitHub Pages) that lets an AI agent look an equation up before using it, plus a human-readable documentation site on the same GitHub Pages deployment. Each entry carries an honest coq_status (closed, definition, wrapped_related, axioms, open_prop, or not_formalisable). Scope: equations and Th_coqc only; papers, books and prose live in their own records and cite Toledo codes.
